ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, points $D$ and $E$ are on $BC$ and $AC$ respectively. $\triangle CDE$ is folded along $DE$ to result in $\triangle FDE$. Lines $BF$ and $CF$ are drawn, with $\angle BFC=90^\circ$. If $EF\parallel AB$, $AB=4\sqrt{3}$, and $EF=10$, what is the length of $AE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, extend $ED$ to meet $CF$ at point $G$,\\
let $\angle BFE=\alpha$\\
By folding, it is known that $DG\perp CF$,\\
since $BF\perp CF$,\\
thus $ED\parallel BF$,\\
therefore $\angle FED=\angle BFE=\alpha$,\\
extend $EA$, $FB$ to meet at point $M$,\\
since $AB\parallel EF$,\\
therefore $\angle BAC=\angle FEC=2\alpha$, $\angle ABM=\angle BFE=\alpha$,\\
therefore $\angle M=\angle BAC-\angle ABM=\alpha$,\\
since $\angle M=\angle BFE=\alpha$, $\angle M=\angle ABM=\alpha$,\\
thus $EM=EF=10$, $AM=AB=4\sqrt{3}$,\\
therefore $AE=EM-AM=10-4\sqrt{3}=\boxed{10-4\sqrt{3}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, points $D$ and $E$ are on $BC$ and $AC$ respectively. $\triangle CDE$ is folded along $DE$ to result in $\triangle FDE$. Lines $BF$ and $CF$ are drawn, with $\angle BFC=90^\circ$. If $EF\parallel AB$, $AB=4\sqrt{3}$, and $EF=10$, what is the length of $AE$?
raw_record.answer:
Solution: As shown in the figure, extend $ED$ to meet $CF$ at point $G$,\\
let $\angle BFE=\alpha$\\
By folding, it is known that $DG\perp CF$,\\
since $BF\perp CF$,\\
thus $ED\parallel BF$,\\
therefore $\angle FED=\angle BFE=\alpha$,\\
extend $EA$, $FB$ to meet at point $M$,\\
since $AB\parallel EF$,\\
therefore $\angle BAC=\angle FEC=2\alpha$, $\angle ABM=\angle BFE=\alpha$,\\
therefore $\angle M=\angle BAC-\angle ABM=\alpha$,\\
since $\angle M=\angle BFE=\alpha$, $\angle M=\angle ABM=\alpha$,\\
thus $EM=EF=10$, $AM=AB=4\sqrt{3}$,\\
therefore $AE=EM-AM=10-4\sqrt{3}=\boxed{10-4\sqrt{3}}$
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure, A is at the upper left, B is on the left side, F is at the lower left, and C is on the right side; E is located on AC, and D is located on BC. The dashed lines represent the original EC and DC, and the solid-line triangle FDE represents the figure after folding. BF and CF are drawn in the figure, and ∠BFC is marked as a right angle at F; EF is parallel to the direction of AB. Then reason: Extend ED to intersect CF at G. Because after triangle CDE is folded along DE, C falls onto F, the crease DE is in the direction of the perpendicular bisector of CF, so ED⊥CF. Also because the problem gives ∠BFC=90°, that is, BF⊥CF, so ED∥BF. Let ∠BFE=α, then from ED∥BF we get ∠FED=α. The folding is symmetric about DE, therefore ED bisects ∠FEC, so ∠FEC=2α. Also EF∥AB, and A, E, C are collinear, so ∠BAC=∠FEC=2α. Extend EA and FB to intersect at M. Since AB∥EF, and MB is collinear with FB, ∠ABM=∠BFE=α. Thus ∠AMB=∠BAC−∠ABM=2α−α=α, therefore in triangle ABM, ∠AMB=∠ABM, giving AM=AB=4√3. At the same time, in triangle MEF, ∠EMF=α and ∠MFE=∠BFE=α, so ME=EF=10. From the order M, A, E on the straight line EA in the figure, AE=ME−AM=10−4√3.
